body.statement: For every finite design and every \(\kappa\ge0\), the set of path tables generated by the maintained model equals \(\mathcal C_\kappa=\operatorname{conv}\{v(q):q\in\Delta(F_\kappa)\}\). The body is compact, and every \(P\in\mathcal C_\kappa\) has an exact rationalization with at most \(m\) fixed-effect mixing types and conditionally iid absolutely continuous shocks supported inside strict response patches.
body.justification: Necessity converts fixed-cell sequential exogeneity and time homogeneity into a mixture of product response probabilities; sufficiency constructs conditionally iid full-vector absolutely continuous shocks inside strict patches.  The exact equality is therefore asserted for the maintained no-tie subclass.
body.gap: Mbakop establishes mixture-of-products geometry and nonpolyhedrality for conditional iid choice bodies, but does not derive the changing-menu switching-cost body or its upper-tail frontier.
body.consumer: Applied researchers can test exact compatibility of a turnover cell without specifying a parametric shock law or a distribution for plan fixed effects.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\kappa\ge0\).  Conditional on \(\lambda\), put \(z_t=\lambda+\epsilon_t\).  For every first-period comparison and every second-period comparison under every possible lag \(a\in M_1\), a tie is an affine hyperplane in \(\mathbb R^J\).  There are finitely many such hyperplanes.  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:absolute-continuity}\) therefore makes their conditional probability zero.  Off their union, the utility index in \(\texttt{ass:utility-index}\) and maximization in \(\texttt{ass:choice-maximization}\) determine one response table
\[
 f(z)=\bigl(f_1(z),(f_2(a;z):a\in M_1)\bigr).
\]
Every designated winner satisfies every strict comparison in \(\texttt{def:comparison-graph}\), so \(f(z)\in F_\kappa\) by \(\texttt{def:feasible-response-set}\).  Define, for almost every \(\lambda\),
\[
 q_f(\lambda)=\Pr\{f(\lambda+\epsilon_t)=f\mid\lambda\},
 \qquad f\in F_\kappa.
\]
Conditional homogeneity makes this definition independent of \(t\), and \(q(\lambda)\in\Delta(F_\kappa)\).

For \(a\in M_1\) and \(b\in M_2\), conditional independence of \(\epsilon_1\) and \(\epsilon_2\), together with the fact that the second-period rule uses the realized lag \(a\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr(Y_1=a,Y_2=b\mid\lambda)
 &=\Pr\{f_1(z_1)=a\mid\lambda\}
   \Pr\{f_2(a;z_2)=b\mid\lambda\}\\
 &=r_a(q(\lambda))s_{ab}(q(\lambda))
 =v_{ab}(q(\lambda)).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the fixed-cell sequential-exogeneity and stationarity factorization used for necessity is exactly
\[
 P=\int v(q(\lambda))\,dF_\lambda(\lambda).
\]
The simplex \(\Delta(F_\kappa)\) is compact and \(v\) is continuous, so its image is compact.  Every image point lies in the affine hyperplane \(\sum_{a,b}x_{ab}=1\), of dimension \(m-1\).  If a convex representation uses more than \(m\) image points, the vectors obtained by adjoining a leading one are linearly dependent; perturbing the convex weights in that null direction until one becomes zero preserves the represented point.  Repetition leaves at most \(m\) image points.  Consequently the convex hull is the continuous image of a compact set of at most \(m\) points and their weights, hence is compact.  Finite simple-function approximations to the displayed integral belong to this convex hull and converge to \(P\); closedness therefore gives \(P\in\mathcal C_\kappa\).

Conversely, take \(P\in\mathcal C_\kappa\).  The same affine-dependence reduction gives
\[
 P=\sum_{\ell=1}^{L_0}\omega_\ell v(q^\ell),
 \qquad 1\le L_0\le m,
 \qquad \omega_\ell\ge0,
 \qquad \sum_{\ell=1}^{L_0}\omega_\ell=1.
\]
For every \(\ell\) and every \(f\) with \(q_f^\ell>0\), \(\texttt{lem:strict-cycle-feasibility}\) supplies an open axis-aligned cube \(B_{\ell f}\) contained in the strict response patch for \(f\).  Let \(G_\ell\) be the probability law assigning mass \(q_f^\ell\) uniformly on \(B_{\ell f}\).  This is an absolutely continuous law on \(\mathbb R^J\).  Choose distinct constants \(c_\ell\), set \(\lambda^\ell=(c_\ell,\ldots,c_\ell)\), and assign \(\Pr(\lambda=\lambda^\ell)=\omega_\ell\).  Conditional on \(\lambda=\lambda^\ell\), draw \(\epsilon_1\) and \(\epsilon_2\) independently from the translate of \(G_\ell\) by \(-\lambda^\ell\).  The two conditional shock laws are identical and absolutely continuous, while \(\lambda^\ell+\epsilon_t\sim G_\ell\).  Hence the conditional response-table law is exactly \(q^\ell\), the conditional path law is \(v(q^\ell)\), and mixing over \(\ell\) produces exactly \(P\).  Every draw lies in a strict patch, so choices are unique.  Zero weights and boundary path probabilities are obtained exactly, without a limiting argument.

The two directions use different class facts.  Necessity uses the fixed-cell conditional factorization supplied by conditional serial independence and conditional time homogeneity, with the no-tie regularity needed to obtain a response table almost surely.  Sufficiency is witnessed by the stronger conditionally iid, full-vector Lebesgue-absolutely-continuous construction just given.  Thus the equality proved here concerns the published fixed-cell model intersected with this explicit no-tie and absolute-continuity subclass, rather than every law in a broader published class.
